data.content_ref: inline:The target's central claim—that the two critics are 'redundant probes of the same latent quality' whose disagreement reflects mere 'calibration misalignment'—is an unsupported assertion that actively mischaracterizes the distinct normative roles the two critic labels encode. 'frontier-claim-honest' and 'frontier-above-floor' name different evaluative axes: honesty concerns whether a frontier claim is faithfully represented, while above-floor concerns whether a claim clears a minimum competence threshold. A claim can be honestly reported yet still fall below floor, or dishonestly inflated yet technically above-floor. The target provides no evidence (and the problem context provides none) that these are operationally identical constructs differing only in stringency. The covering principle 'construct-identity under divergent operationalization' is therefore stipulated, not established, and the conclusion that the ritual 'perpetually flags one or the other' as a calibration artifact is unsubstantiated by the artifact's own content.
